questions.q: Programming languages belong to which category of computer software?
questions.e: The lesson calls programming languages the third category of computer software.

questions.q: What are programming languages used for?
o: Writing programs, scripts, and instructions that a computer can execute
questions.e: Programmers use them to write executable instructions.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the main difference between programming languages?
questions.e: Programming languages share similarities; the main difference is syntax.

questions.q: First generation languages are essentially written in what?
Machine language code is made up of what?
o: A series of zeros and ones
questions.e: Machine code is binary: zeros and ones.

questions.q: First generation languages are classified as what?
questions.e: 1GL are low-level languages close to machine code.

questions.q: Second generation languages are best described as what?
Where are second generation languages commonly used according to the lesson?
questions.e: Assembly is used in kernels and hardware drivers.

questions.q: In which decade did second generation languages become popular?
What does assembly language use in place of binary numbers?
questions.e: Structured commands make assembly easier to read than binary.

questions.q: What tool converts assembly language statements into machine language?
questions.e: An assembler translates assembly into machine code.

questions.q: Third generation languages are also known as what?
Which of the following is a third generation language?
questions.e: C++ is a high-level 3GL; SQL is 4GL and Prolog is 5GL.

questions.q: Why are high-level languages easier to understand?
questions.e: English-type keywords make high-level code readable.

questions.q: What must happen before a 3GL program can execute?
o: The source program must be translated to binary using an interpreter or compiler
It must be uploaded to a database
It must be converted to assembly by hand
questions.e: 3GL source code must be translated to machine-readable binary.

questions.q: Fourth generation languages consist of what?
o: English-type statements similar to human language

questions.q: Fourth generation languages are used mainly for what?
questions.e: 4GL are used in database programming and scripting.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fourth generation language?
questions.e: SQL is a 4GL used for database queries.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fourth generation language from the lesson?
questions.e: The lesson lists Python, Ruby, Perl, SQL, and MATLAB as 4GL.

questions.q: What do fifth generation languages use to develop programs?
questions.e: 5GL provide visual tools for program development.

questions.q: Which is an example of a fifth generation language?
questions.e: Mercury, OPS5, and Prolog are 5GL examples.

questions.q: Machine language belongs to which generation?
Assembly language belongs to which generation?
Java belongs to which generation of languages?
According to the lesson, Python belongs to which generation?
questions.e: Python is classified as a 4GL in the lesson.

questions.q: Mercury is an example of which generation?
Pascal belongs to which generation?
Ruby is classified in the lesson as which generation?
OPS5 is an example of which generation?
BASIC belongs to which generation?
JavaScript belongs to which generation?
MATLAB is classified as which generation?
Which tool is used with a second generation language?
questions.e: An assembler converts assembly to machine language.

questions.q: Which translation tools are mentioned for executing 3GL programs?
questions.e: 3GL programs use an interpreter or compiler.

questions.q: Which generation is the lowest-level language?
questions.e: 1GL machine language is the lowest level.

questions.q: Which generation uses statements most similar to human language?
Which generation is characterized by visual tools?
A programmer writing low-level code for a hardware driver would most likely use which generation?
questions.e: Assembly (2GL) is used in kernels and hardware drivers.

questions.q: Which pairing of language and generation is correct?
questions.e: SQL is 4GL; Prolog is 5GL; assembly is 2GL.

questions.q: Which pairing of language and generation is INCORRECT?
What can be executed directly by the computer's processor?
questions.e: Machine code is the binary form the CPU executes.

questions.q: What is source code?
o: The human-readable code written by a programmer
questions.e: Source code is written by programmers and then translated.

questions.q: How does a compiler differ from an interpreter?
o: A compiler runs only in browsers
A compiler translates the whole program before execution; an interpreter translates line by line
questions.e: Compilers translate the program as a whole; interpreters work line by line.

questions.q: What is the output of an assembler?
questions.e: The assembler converts assembly statements into machine language.

questions.q: A program written in C is an example of what?
questions.e: C code is human-readable source code before translation.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a third generation language?
Which of these is NOT a fourth generation language?
Which of these is NOT a fifth generation language?
Which language is mainly used for database queries?
questions.e: SQL is a 4GL for database programming.

questions.q: Why is assembly easier to read than binary?
o: It uses structured commands instead of raw binary numbers
questions.e: Structured commands are more human-readable than binary.

questions.q: A developer wants to write database scripts quickly using English-like statements. Which generation is best?
A class is learning with a readable, high-level language like Java. Which generation is Java?
A programmer needs direct control of hardware using symbolic instructions. Which generation fits?
A developer builds a program by connecting visual blocks rather than typing text. This matches which generation?
Which sequence arranges generations from lowest to highest level?
questions.e: Numbers increase with abstraction and ease of use.

questions.q: Which statement about syntax is correct?
o: Programming languages share similarities but differ in syntax
questions.e: The lesson notes similarity across languages with syntax as the difference.

questions.q: Which is an example of a low-level language?
Which list contains ONLY fourth generation languages from the lesson?
questions.e: The 4GL list is Perl, Python, Ruby, SQL, and MATLAB.

questions.q: Why must 3GL source code be translated before execution?
o: The OS cannot read file names
Compilers are required for internet access
The processor executes binary machine code, not source text
questions.e: CPUs execute machine code, so source must be converted to binary.

questions.q: Which pairing is correct for the translation tool of each generation?
What is the third category of computer software used to write programs and instructions?
questions.e: Programming languages form the third software category.

questions.q: What is the low-level language written as binary code called?
What language uses structured commands in place of binary numbers?
What program converts assembly language into machine language?
What generation includes high-level languages like C, C++, Java, and Pascal?
What type of program translates source code into binary form?
questions.e: Compilers and interpreters translate source code.

questions.q: What generation consists of English-type statements and is used in database programming?
What generation provides visual tools to develop programs?
Name one fifth generation language.
Name the fourth generation query language used with databases.
questions.e: SQL is the classic 4GL database query language.

questions.q: Name one third generation language.
questions.e: 3GL examples include C, C++, Java, Pascal, BASIC, and JavaScript.

questions.q: What do we call the human-readable code written by a programmer?
questions.e: Source code is the input to a compiler or interpreter.

questions.q: What do we call the binary instructions executed by the processor?
questions.e: Machine code is directly executed by the CPU.

questions.q: What translation tool converts the entire program before it runs?
questions.e: A compiler translates the whole program before execution.

questions.q: What translation tool translates and executes code line by line?
questions.e: An interpreter works line by line.

questions.q: In which decade did second generation languages become popular?
What is another name for first generation language?
What is another name for second generation language?
Which 4GL is named after its matrix laboratory purpose?
Which 4GL scripting language is named after a gemstone?
Which 3GL was developed by Bjarne Stroustrup as an extension of C?
questions.e: C++ extends C with object-oriented features.

questions.q: Which 3GL was created by Sun Microsystems and runs on the Java Virtual Machine?
Which 4GL scripting language was created by Larry Wall?
Which 5GL is commonly associated with artificial intelligence and logic programming?
Which 3GL is known as a beginner-friendly language with the keyword PRINT and was developed at Dartmouth?
questions.e: BASIC is a 3GL designed for beginners.

Second generation languages use an assembler to convert statements to machine language.
Assembly language is [[harder to read]] than raw binary code.
questions.e: Structured commands make assembly easier to read than binary.

questions.q: Third generation languages include Java and C++.
Third generation programs can [[run directly without any translation]].
questions.e: 3GL source must be translated to binary first.

questions.q: Fourth generation languages are used mainly in database programming and scripting.
In the lesson, Python is classified as a [[fifth generation]] language.
Fifth generation languages use visual tools to develop programs.
questions.e: Visual tools are the defining feature of 5GL.

questions.q: Prolog is an example of a fifth generation language.
[[A compiler]] translates a program one line at a time while it runs.
